drivingQuestion: How do we know כפות תמרים refers to the lulav, and how many are required?
outcomeNote: the lulav is identified as a single bindable palm branch

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי ״כַּפּוֹת תְּמָרִים״ דְּלוּלַבָּא הוּא? אֵימָא חֲרוּתָא! בָּעֵינָא כְּפוֹת וְלֵיכָּא.
segments.en: «Ravina said to Rav Ashi: From where» is it ascertained «that this» term, «“branches of a date palm,” is» referring to the branches «of the lulav? Say» it is referring to «the hardened branch» of the date palm. Rav Ashi answered: That cannot be, as «we require» the lulav «to be bound, and there is no» binding, since at that stage the hardened leaves point outward, and binding them is impossible.

segments.he: וְאֵימָא אוּפְתָּא! ״כְּפוֹת״ — מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא פָּרוּד, וְהַאי כָּפוּת וְעוֹמֵד לְעוֹלָם.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: If the fundamental requirement of the mitzva is a lulav that appears as one unit, «say» that one takes «the trunk» of the date palm. The Gemara answers: The term «bound,» from which it is derived that the branch should appear as one unit, «indicates that there is» the possibility that it could be «spread. However, this» trunk «is perpetually bound,» as it can never become separated.

segments.he: וְאֵימָא כּוּפְרָא? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: ״דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי נוֹעַם וְכׇל נְתִיבוֹתֶיהָ שָׁלוֹם״ כְּתִיב.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And say» the verse is referring to «the branch of the date palm [kufra]» that has not yet hardened completely and could still be bound, albeit with difficulty. «Abaye said» that «it is written» in praise of the Torah: «“Its way are ways of pleasantness and all its paths are peace”» (Proverbs 3:17). At that stage of development, some of the leaves are thorns that potentially wound. The Torah would not command to use that type of branch in fulfilling the mitzva.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא תּוֹסְפָאָה לְרָבִינָא: וְאֵימָא תַּרְתֵּי כַּפֵּי דְתַמְרֵי? ״כַּפַּת״ כְּתִיב. וְאֵימָא חֲדָא? לְהָהוּא — ״כַּף״ קָרֵי לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Rava, the expert in Tosefta, said to Ravina:» Since the verse states “branches of a date palm” in the plural, «say» that one is obligated to take «two palm branches» in fulfilling the mitzva of the four species. Ravina answered: Although the word is vocalized in the plural, based on tradition «kappot is written» without the letter vav, indicating that only one is required. The Gemara suggests: «And say» that one is required to take only «one» leaf? The Gemara answers: If that were the intention of the Torah, it would not have written kappot without a vav. «That» single leaf «is called kaf.» Kappot without the vav indicates both plural, i.e., multiple leaves, and singular, i.e., one branch.
